title: Option Type Pattern
snippet: Handle nullable values safely with Maybe<T>
description: Maybe<T> (also called Option<T> in BPL's stdlib) is a type-safe way to represent values that might be absent, replacing nullptrs. It's an enum with two variants: Some(T) containing a value, or None representing absence. This eliminates nullptr errors at compile time by forcing explicit handling of missing values. Pattern matching on Maybe makes the intent clear and prevents forgetting to check for nullptr. Common patterns include unwrapping with defaults, chaining operations, and mapping over optional values. This example uses a custom Maybe<T> to demonstrate the pattern - in real code, use Option<T> from std/option.bpl.
